newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds weaken after surprise UK rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds weaken after surprise UK rate rise.

text.p: Irish government bonds weakened in active afternoon trade on Wednesday as the punt slipped against sterling following a surprise 25 basis point rate rise in the UK, dealers said.

The minimum lending rate was raised by a quarter-point to 6.0 percent following the monthly monetary meeting between the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Kenneth Clarke, and the governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George.
"The Irish curve has flattened quite a bit following the news from the UK," one dealer said. "Sterling/Irish levels have weakened which puts the Irish Central Bank under pressure."
By 1620 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000, which touched 106.64 earlier in the day, had eased 20p from Tuesday's close to 106.25 to yield 6.09 percent.
The eight percent bond due 2006 was down five pence from the close at 107.50 to yield 6.80 having traded at 107.90 earlier.
The Irish pound eased to 1.0025 sterling from 1.0090 against sterling at Tuesday's close.
"The punt weakening in this way will put a lot of pressure on the Irish Central Bank in terms of inflationary numbers," the dealer said.
